A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same R-TPT research work, with complete main text and supplementary material. All 12 pages in each version were inspected, including equations, figures, tables, references, and the supplementary algorithm and experiments.

before.justification: Sections 4 and 8 report original experiments on CLIP adaptation and adversarial robustness, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: The original empirical evaluations remain, with revised Aircraft adversarial accuracies and associated aggregate results in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: Section 3 and supplementary Algorithm 1 retain the same pointwise entropy minimization, neighbor-based reliability calculation, and weighted prediction ensembling. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight fine-grained datasets, ImageNet, and four ImageNet distribution-shift benchmarks listed in Table 8. Clean and adversarial test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within each experiment: CLIP, Ensemble, TPT, C-TPT, and MTA in the adaptation comparisons, and the same TeCoA, APT, and FARE configurations in the supplementary training-time comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported backbones, attack-generation procedures, PGD radii and steps, adaptation budgets, metrics, and dataset sizes are unchanged. The numerical revisions are not accompanied by a reported protocol change or statement that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 7 revises the quantitative evidence for the existing component ablation: weighted ensembling without entropy minimization changes from 44.3% to 43.6% fine-grained adversarial accuracy, and the full method from 45.8% to 45.2%. The tested configurations and questions remain unchanged, as do the other robustness and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Revisions are concentrated in Aircraft adversarial accuracies in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 9–11, their averages, and Table 7. For example, Table 1 changes R-TPT's Aircraft result from 17.5% to 12.6% and its average from 45.8% to 45.2%; Table 9 changes these from 31.7% to 17.2% and 51.4% to 49.6%. Aircraft rankings change, but clean accuracies, other dataset results, and the overall ordering of test-time methods by average robustness remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the marginal-entropy decomposition and reliability definition, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims: test-time adversarial defense for CLIP without labeled training data, using pointwise entropy minimization and reliability-based ensembling.

C2.justification: The explanations of optimization conflicts, unreliable views, clean-accuracy tradeoffs, and inference costs are unchanged. The discussion does not reinterpret the revised results and retains numerical statements that now disagree with Tables 1 and 4.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including prompt initialization and length, learning rate, augmented batch size, optimizer, PyTorch, RTX3090 hardware, and the code repository link. No explanation of the numerical revisions is added.

R1.justification: The 62 references and related-work discussion are unchanged, including the positioning relative to training-time defenses and existing test-time adaptation methods.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 15 April 2025 to v2 dated 27 August 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Best-result highlighting moves with the revised Aircraft rankings: from MTA to R-TPT in Tables 1, 2, and 9, and from TPT to R-TPT in Table 4. Figures, captions, table structures, and page organization remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision addresses an apparent systematic duplication of clean accuracies in the Aircraft robustness columns and updates associated averages and ablation results, providing a limited improvement in empirical reporting. However, it introduces table-text inconsistencies: Section 4.2 still reports 45.8% instead of Table 1's 45.2%, and Section 4.3 retains 13.1% to 21.7% instead of Table 4's 12.3% to 21.2%. These omissions limit the benefit.
